This is then metabolized in the liver to 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 (calcifediol). The next step occurs in the kidneys, where 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 is converted to the active form, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 (calcitriol), by the enzyme 1-alpha-hydroxylase. This enzyme is considered the rate-limiting step in the synthesis of the active form of vitamin D.
